title: QC: read the evidence, not just the headline
description: Read genuine downloaded and computed quality reports, distinguish missing checks from warnings and failures, and find the three nested QC tools.
objectives: Find QC and its nested tools.
Select the exact project or bounded-run folder and inspect all five evidence categories.
Distinguish missing, warning and failure results without assuming a dashboard validates an entire analysis.
Refresh existing evidence without recomputing or changing the source files.
prerequisite: Download the Annotate and Mask examples first. This recording reuses Annotate's measurement database, the original Mask example scorecards, and the genuine two-field Mask/one-field Measure tutorial run in plate1/test. QC itself downloads nothing and performs no new scoring. The parent and test folders represent different evidence scopes, not a before/after improvement experiment.

scenes.narration: Open QC in Home's Data category. This dashboard reads quality reports already on disk. It does not generate masks, measure images or train a classifier. The headline summarises available evidence; it is not a certificate that an entire analysis is correct.

The header groups Layer Viewer, Control Charts and Outliers under QC. Their specialist lessons remain in the Submodules section beneath this parent. Use those tools to investigate an observation, not to replace missing evidence with a reassuring dashboard colour.

Use Browse to select the actual project folder. We first open Annotate's downloaded example, which contains measurements but no segmentation scorecards in this folder. QC has no separate example downloader; reuse the real project from the earlier workflow.

Missing means the reader has no usable report for that check. It is neither a pass nor proof that a check failed. A calculation performed in another view may not have saved a report this dashboard can read. Always inspect the named source and scope.

Now choose the test subfolder containing our genuine bounded Mask and Measure outputs. Selecting the parent folder is not equivalent. These are different populations and artifacts, so their verdicts must not be presented as a controlled before-and-after comparison.

The subset reports a segmentation warning: one cell field has a heterogeneous size distribution. Read the guidance and inspect the images. A size-based flag does not establish two biological cell types or prove that every object boundary is wrong.

The units card reports internal consistency across four measurement tables. That is narrower than independently validating calibration or every feature. Leakage, plate effects and annotator agreement still lack reports here; the green units card does not make those missing checks pass.

Read all five categories, including the guidance below missing cards. Retain the original reports and investigate the relevant workflow. In particular, a leakage verdict depends on correct sample identities and grouping; a software pass alone cannot establish biological independence.

The downloaded full-plate scorecards show failures as well as warnings. The headline names a low-count pathogen field, and the detail lists other flags. These are existing reports from the broader example, not new scores computed by opening QC or evidence that our smaller run improved the plate.

Press Refresh after reviewing the source. Here the status says nothing on disk has changed, so the existing evidence is reused. Refresh is not Run: it neither rescored the masks nor repaired a warning. Our database and report hashes remain unchanged.

An out-of-date label, when present, needs attention to the underlying report and its inputs. This dashboard is advisory and does not block a run. Its cards are explanatory text, not buttons that automatically open or repair every failing analysis.

For a scripted read, spacr.qt.widgets.qc_summary provides read_dashboard and format_dashboard. They assemble existing evidence rather than running new checks. Keep the source reports with the project, and return to the relevant analysis or specialist lesson for the investigation itself.
